To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fluorescence and gain line shape in laser dye mixures can be predicted using a theoretical model based on the Forster theory of radiative energy transfer.

the fluorescence and gain predictions in three different laser mixtures of (1) Dichlorofluorescin (DCF, donor) and DODCI (acceptor), 2) DCF (donor) with Rhodamine B (RhB, acceptor), and 3) Coumarin (donor, C-480) and RhB are generally in excellent quantitative agreement with experimental results.

the steady state fluorescence of dye mixtures can be predicted using computer simulation, and this is a practical approach for predicting fluorescence emission spectra and gain line shapes of dye mixtures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theoretical model to describe the fluorescence and gain characteristics of laser dye mixures and the experimental verification of the theoretical predictions.
the development of new and improved laser dye mixtures for tunable solid state dye lasers and the development of a new method to predict fluorescence spectra and gain lineshapes of dye mixtures.
developing an analytical method for predicting steady state fluorescence and gain line shape of dye mixtures under steady state excitaion conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the radiative energy transfer in dye mixtures can be effectively used to predict fluorescence spectra as well as gain lineshape and hence tunability of laser dye mixtured under steady state conditions.
fluorescence and gain predictions of laser dyes mixtures can be made with a reasonable degree of accuracy.

the fluorescence and gain predictions derived from the analytical expressions developed in this thesis are in excellent agreement with the experimental results, and the analytical approach developed is a very useful and effective method to predict the fluorescence emission spectra and gain lineshapes of laser dye mixtues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

radiative energy transfer is the dominant mechanism in the three different dye mixtures studied and that the theoretical predictions derived are effective in predicting the fluorescence emission spectra and hence the laser gain lineshape of dye mixtures.
radiative energy transfer is the dominant process for energy transfer in dye mixtures at the concentrations needed for lacing.
the method is useful and effective for the design of laser dye mixtues for tunable lasers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to predict laser gain lineshape of dye mixtures by knowing the absorption and emission spectra of the dyes and their concentrations in the mixture.
radiative transfer in dye mixtures can be predicted using simple expressions and computer simulation.

the fluorescence spectra of dye mixtues can be predicted using our model, and the gain spectrum is the convolution of fluorescence spectra of the individual dyes in the mixture, weighted by their concentrations.
